comment: The generated coordinates themselves are not regression tested. They are
the output of a floating point minimisation and vary in the last digit
with compiler, platform and optimisation level, so golden molfiles would
fail spuriously - the same reason the repo warns to build -c opt before
running these tests. The layout geometry is tested instead by the unit
tests in src/Depict/coords_2d_test.cc, which assert properties (bond
lengths, no coincident atoms, benzene is a regular hexagon) rather than
coordinate values. What is regression tested here is the tool's file
level behaviour.
A molfile that cannot be read back is useless, so the structures are
round tripped through fileconv and the smiles compared. Note that this
shows a round trip within LillyMol, not that stereochemistry is conveyed
to other software: nicotine keeps its chirality because LillyMol carries
it in the MDL atom parity field and reads that back, whereas other
toolkits ignore parity on a 2D record and want wedge bonds. Wedges are
what the wedge_bonds case below is about.
test.name: roundtrip

comment: LillyMol's default molfile counts line is abbreviated, and some toolkits
refuse to read it. Since the whole point of generating coordinates is
that other software can use them, this tool writes full V2000 records,
and -t restores the terse form. Guards against a change in the option
processing order silently dropping the full records: the -t flag has to
be examined before the -o options are processed.
test.name: counts_line

comment: Chirality reaches other software only through wedge bonds, so this checks
the wedges written for a set of stereocentres - acyclic, in a ring,
quaternary, bridged, and five in one molecule - reading them straight out
of the molfile rather than through another toolkit's interpretation.
Two properties matter and both are visible in the golden file. A wedge's
narrow end has to be its first atom in the bond block, otherwise readers
that take the first atom as the stereocentre, RDKit among them, discard
it; that is cross checked against the parity field, which says which
atoms LillyMol considers chiral. And the sense has to be derived from the
layout rather than guessed, which is why both enantiomers of alanine are
here: they are drawn identically and so must be wedged oppositely.
cis_dimethylcyclohexane is marked chiral in its smiles but is not
stereogenic, both ring branches from each centre being identical. Drawing
no wedge is the right answer, not a failure.
test.name: wedge_bonds

comment: Cis/trans is the one piece of stereochemistry a molfile has no field for:
it lives only in which side of the double bond each substituent is drawn
on. The layout engine left to itself draws every double bond trans, so
without the constraint every Z double bond is silently written as E. This
lays the structures out, reads the configuration back out of the
coordinates with fileconv -i dctb, and compares the smiles.
The -z output is in the golden file as the control: it is the raw engine
layout, where the cis structures come back as their trans isomers. And
the third block reads the same file without -i dctb, which is how
LillyMol reads a molfile by default and shows that it derives no
cis/trans at all - the depiction is correct either way, but a reader has
to ask for it.
test.name: cis_trans
